subject: Film & Cinema
title: Point of View: Whose Eyes?
description: A fast breakdown of Point of View: Whose Eyes? for builders.

hook.text: Every shot is someone's perspective. Choosing whose eyes to use changes the entire story.

buildup.text: Objective shots observe from outside. Subjective POV shots put you inside a character's head.

discovery.text: Hitchcock used POV to make audiences complicit — you see what the voyeur sees in Rear Window.

twist.text: Shifting POV mid-scene can disorient the viewer, creating unease without any dialogue.

climax.text: Visual POV is cinema's most direct tool for building empathy or suspicion.

punchline.text: Whose eyes you borrow shapes what you feel.

quiz.question: How did Hitchcock use POV in Rear Window?
options: To make the audience complicit by sharing the voyeur's perspective
